1 مَغَثَ , (S,) aor.
مَغُثَ , (TK,) inf. n. مَغْثٌ, (K,) He steeped, soaked, or macerated, a thing in water, and rubbed it with the fingers; he steeped it in water, and mashed it with the hand; (TA;) he steeped, and mashed with the hand, medicine in water; syn. مَرَثَ. (S, K. *) ―
-b2- مَغَثَ المَطَرُ الكَلَأَ inf. n. مَغْثٌ, The rain fell upon the herbage, and rendered it yellow, and bad-tasted, and laid it prostrate. (TA.) ―
-b3- مَغَثَ, [aor.
مَغُثَ ,] He submerged, or immersed, him, or it, in water. (K.) ―
-b4- مُغِثَ He was affected by a fever. (TA.) ―
-b5- مَغَثَتْهُ الحُمَّى The fever attacked him; or pained him. (TA.) ―
-b6- مَغَثُوهُ, [aor.
مَغُثَ ,] (S,) inf. n. مَغَثٌ, (K,) They beat him lightly, (S, K, *) as though they shook him about (كَأَنَّهُمْ تَلْتَلُوهُ). (S.) ―
-b7- مَغَثَ عِرْضَهُ, (inf. n. مَغْثٌ, K,) He defamed him; disgraced him; dishonoured him; (S, K;) aspersed him by reviling. (TA.) ―
-b8- مَغَثَهُمْ بِشَرٍّ He did evil to them. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
